requirements.quote:
NEW_CONNECTION_ID Frame {
     Type (i) = 0x18,
     Sequence Number (i),
     Retire Prior To (i),
     Length (8),
     Connection ID (8..160),
     Stateless Reset Token (128),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and recognize the frame Type as the variable-length integer value 0x18.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a different Type value as a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame type and its fixed value can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
NEW_CONNECTION_ID Frame {
     Type (i) = 0x18,
     Sequence Number (i),
     Retire Prior To (i),
     Length (8),
     Connection ID (8..160),
     Stateless Reset Token (128),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Place and parse the fields in this order: Type, Sequence Number, Retire Prior To, Length, Connection ID, Stateless Reset Token.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder or omit the listed fields.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized frame can be checked for the exact listed field sequence and presence.

requirements.quote:
Sequence Number:  The sequence number assigned to the connection ID
      by the sender, encoded as a variable-length integer; see
      Section 5.1.1.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the Sequence Number field.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the sender-assigned sequence number for the connection ID as a variable-length integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The field encoding and association with the connection ID can be checked in serialized frames and sender state.

requirements.quote:
Retire Prior To:  A variable-length integer indicating which
      connection IDs should be retired; see Section 5.1.2.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the Retire Prior To field.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Retire Prior To as a variable-length integer whose value indicates which connection IDs should be retired.
requirements.why_checkable: The wire encoding and interpreted retirement threshold can be directly tested.

requirements.quote:
Length:  An 8-bit unsigned integer containing the length of the
      connection ID.  Values less than 1 and greater than 20 are invalid
      and MUST be treated as a connection error of type
      FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Length field of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Length as an 8-bit unsigned integer containing the connection ID length, with a valid value from 1 through 20 inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept a Length value less than 1 or greater than 20 as valid.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat a Length value less than 1 or greater than 20 as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary-value frames can verify the field width, accepted interval, and exact error classification.

requirements.quote: Connection ID:  A connection ID of the specified length.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Connection ID field.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or consume exactly the number of Connection ID bytes specified by the Length field.
requirements.why_checkable: The Connection ID byte count can be compared directly with the decoded Length value.

requirements.quote:
Stateless Reset Token:  A 128-bit value that will be used for a
      stateless reset when the associated connection ID is used; see
      Section 10.3.
requirements.condition: When encoding, storing, or using the Stateless Reset Token from a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the token as a 128-bit value and associate it with the frame's connection ID for stateless reset use when that connection ID is used.
requirements.why_checkable: The token width and its stored association with a connection ID can be inspected and exercised.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT send this frame if it currently requires that
   its peer send packets with a zero-length Destination Connection ID.
requirements.condition: If an endpoint currently requires its peer to send packets with a zero-length Destination Connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not send a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish the zero-length Destination Connection ID requirement and observe whether the endpoint transmits this frame.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that is sending packets with a zero-length Destination
   Connection ID MUST treat receipt of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame as a
   connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sending packets with a zero-length Destination Connection ID receives a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or process the received frame as valid.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's connection-error response and exact error type can be observed after injecting the frame.

requirements.quote:

   of the same frame multiple times MUST NOT be treated as a connection
   error.  A receiver can use the sequence number supplied in the
requirements.condition: When the same NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame is received multiple times.
requirements.required_behavior: Tolerate duplicate receipt without treating it as a connection error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat repeated receipt of the same frame as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver an identical frame repeatedly and observe whether a connection error is raised.

requirements.quote:
If an endpoint receives a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame that repeats a
   previously issued connection ID with a different Stateless Reset
   Token field value or a different Sequence Number field value, or if a
   sequence number is used for different connection IDs, the endpoint
   MAY treat that receipt as a connection error of type
   PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When a received NEW_CONNECTION_ID repeats a previously issued connection ID with a different Stateless Reset Token or a different Sequence Number, or reuses one sequence number for different connection IDs.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: Stored connection-ID, token, and sequence mappings can be compared with an injected inconsistent frame, and any resulting error type can be verified.

requirements.quote:
The Retire Prior To field applies to connection IDs established
   during connection setup and the preferred_address transport
   parameter; see Section 5.1.2.  The value in the Retire Prior To field
   MUST be less than or equal to the value in the Sequence Number field.
requirements.condition: When applying the Retire Prior To value from a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the retirement threshold to connection IDs established during connection setup and through the preferred_address transport parameter.
requirements.why_checkable: Receiver state can be populated from both named sources and checked for application of the retirement threshold.

requirements.quote:

   MUST be less than or equal to the value in the Sequence Number field.
   Receiving a value in the Retire Prior To field that is greater than
   that in the Sequence Number field MUST be treated as a connection
   error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When encoding or receiving a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure Retire Prior To is less than or equal to Sequence Number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept Retire Prior To greater than Sequence Number as valid.
requirements.error_behavior: On receipt of Retire Prior To greater than Sequence Number, treat it as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames covering both sides of the numeric boundary can verify the invariant and exact error response.

requirements.quote:
Once a sender indicates a Retire Prior To value, smaller values sent
   in subsequent NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames have no effect.  A receiver
   MUST ignore any Retire Prior To fields that do not increase the
   largest received Retire Prior To value.
requirements.condition: When a subsequent NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame has a Retire Prior To value that does not exceed the largest Retire Prior To value previously received.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the non-increasing Retire Prior To field and preserve the effect of the largest received value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reduce or reapply the effective retirement threshold based on a non-increasing value.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of frames with increasing, equal, and decreasing values can verify the receiver's retained threshold and retirement state.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that receives a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with a sequence
   number smaller than the Retire Prior To field of a previously
   received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST send a corresponding
   RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame that retires the newly received connection
   ID, unless it has already done so for that sequence number.
requirements.condition: When a received NEW_CONNECTION_ID has a sequence number smaller than a Retire Prior To value from a previously received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame, and the endpoint has not already retired that sequence number.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame that retires the newly received connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send another corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame if one has already been sent for that sequence number.
requirements.why_checkable: A stateful test can establish a prior retirement threshold, inject an older sequence number, and verify both required first transmission and duplicate suppression.
